systems.name: Hartree atomic units (SI-based rendering, 4πε₀ = 1)
systems.used_in: Essentially all of quantum chemistry (Gaussian, ORCA, Molpro, Psi4, PySCF, NWChem, Turbomole, Dalton, CFOUR), electronic-structure codes ABINIT/CP2K/BigDFT, AMO theory, attosecond and strong-field physics, ab initio molecular dynamics. This is the default internal unit system of nearly every quantum-chemistry program.

Total energies with 6-10 decimals and magnitudes ~ -76.24 (H₂O), -1.174 (H₂), -128.9 (Ne)
Words: hartree, E_h, bohr, a₀, millihartree, mE_h, microhartree, "chemical accuracy"

Strong-field AMO: field amplitudes like "E₀ = 0.05 a.u.", intensity 3.51×10¹⁶ W/cm², "24 as" time unit, ponderomotive U_p = I/(4ω²)
Dipole moments in a.u. converted with 2.541746 D

TRAP 1 — temperature is NOT fixed. The four generators span only (M, L, T, I); Θ is untouched. A paper writing "T = 0.001" in atomic units means 0.001 E_h/k_B = 315.8 K, but many AMO papers quote T in kelvin inside otherwise-atomic-units text. If k_B = 1 is also intended, it must be declared separately (see the k_B = 1 entry).

TRAP 2 — atomic unit of intensity. I₀ = ½ε₀cE_au² = 3.50944553e16 W/cm². A substantial minority of papers omit the ½ and quote 7.019e16 W/cm²; the ratio is a silent factor of 2 in every reported intensity.

TRAP 3 — nuclear masses. m_e = 1, but chemists supply masses in u: 1 u = 1822.888486278 m_e. Getting this wrong scales vibrational frequencies by √1822.9 ≈ 42.7. LAMMPS "units electron" is a deliberate HYBRID (hartree energy + bohr length + femtosecond time + amu mass) and is NOT a consistent atomic-unit system — a real detection hazard.

TRAP 4 — magnetism. Everything ELECTRIC above is identical in the Gaussian rendering, but every MAGNETIC quantity differs by a factor of α ≈ 1/137. See the separate Gaussian-based entry; "1 a.u. of magnetic field" is genuinely ambiguous between 2.3505e5 T and 1.7153e3 T.

HISTORY — Hartree (Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 24, 89 (1928)) defined "the unit of energy e²/a₀", which is today's hartree = 2 Ry. Some pre-1960 literature says "atomic units" while quoting energies in rydberg; do not trust the phrase alone.

Minor variants worth flagging: relativistic quantum-chemistry codes fix c = 137.0359998 or 137.03599976 (older CODATA); the difference is below any chemical significance but changes 10th-decimal benchmark energies. "Atomic units" plus k_B = 1 plus c = 1 is NOT self-consistent — c = 1 forces e = √α (see the relativistic entry).

systems.name: Hartree atomic units (Gaussian/cgs-based rendering)
aliases: atomic units with explicit 1/c in magnetic terms
systems.used_in: Atomic-structure and atomic-spectroscopy theory (Cowan's RCN/RCG/RCE, Condon–Shortley and Sobelman lineage, GRASP/MCDHF write-ups), older AMO literature, plasma spectroscopy, much of the Russian-language atomic-physics literature, and any paper that says "Gaussian units" or "cgs" in the same breath as "atomic units".

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: B_{\rm Gauss\text{-}a.u.} = c\,B_{\rm SI\text{-}a.u.} = \alpha^{-1} B_{\rm SI\text{-}a.u.};\ \text{equivalently the Gaussian a.u. of }B\text{ is }\alpha\times 2.35051757077\times10^{5}\,\mathrm{T} = 1.7152555\times10^{3}\,\mathrm{T} = 1.7152555\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{G} = e/a_0^2
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Gaussian electrodynamics puts 1/c in the Lorentz force (F = q(E + v×B/c)), so B carries the same dimension as E. The atomic unit of B is then e/a₀² rather than ħ/(ea₀²), and the two differ by exactly α.
μ_B = eħ/(2m_e c) in Gaussian vs eħ/(2m_e) in SI. The product μ·B is convention-independent, which is why the two errors cancel in energies but not in reported field or moment values.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: q_{\rm Gaussian} = q_{\rm SI}/\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0};\ \dim q = M^{1/2}L^{3/2}T^{-1} \Rightarrow (0.5,\,1.5,\,-1,\,0,\,0)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: There is no independent current dimension; charge is derived from F = q²/r². This is where half-integer exponents enter the family.

fingerprints: Explicit 1/c or 1/c² in magnetic and relativistic terms: H_Z = (1/2c)(L + 2S)·B; diamagnetic term (1/8c²)B²(x²+y²); spin-orbit ζ = (1/2c²)(1/r)(dV/dr)
Minimal coupling written (p + A/c)²/2 rather than (p + A)²/2
Maxwell equations quoted as ∇×B = (4π/c)J + (1/c)∂E/∂t
Breit–Pauli operators with 1/c² prefactors where SI-based atomic units would write α²
Magnetic fields quoted in gauss with the atomic unit stated as 1.7153×10⁷ G or 1715 T
The phrases "Gaussian atomic units", "cgs atomic units", or a units table listing both e and c

systems.notes:
This is not a different unit system in the ordinary sense — it is the SAME system with a different electromagnetic symbol convention grafted on. Every purely electric quantity (energy, length, dipole, polarizability, electric field, potential) has IDENTICAL numerical values in the two renderings. Every magnetic quantity differs by a power of α ≈ 1/137.036.

The practical consequence for the tool: a bare statement "in atomic units, B = 0.1" is UNRESOLVABLE without reading the Hamiltonian. 0.1 a.u. is either 2.35×10⁴ T (SI-based) or 171.5 T (Gaussian-based) — a factor of 137. The only reliable discriminator is whether magnetic terms carry an explicit 1/c. Recommend the tool emit a warning rather than a conversion when a magnetic quantity in "a.u." appears without that evidence.

Dimensionally, this rendering has three generators spanning (M, L, T) only, with charge derived as M^½L^{3/2}T⁻¹. Determinant of the generator matrix over (M,L,T) is 1/2 ≠ 0, so the system is well-posed; but the I exponent is identically zero and half-integers appear throughout the electric sector. A tool must support BOTH the 4-generator integer-exponent rendering and this 3-generator half-integer one, and must know they are the same physical system.

A Heaviside–Lorentz-rationalized atomic-unit variant (where ∇·E = ρ and e² = 4πα in relativistic form) is essentially absent from AMO literature; I have not found it used and would not implement it.

systems.name: Rydberg atomic units
systems.used_in: Plane-wave pseudopotential DFT (Quantum ESPRESSO/PWscf, older PWSCF-lineage and pseudopotential-generation codes, ELK partially, Abinit's Ry output options), solid-state electronic structure, electron–atom and electron–molecule scattering theory (cross sections in πa₀², energies in Ry), older atomic-physics literature (Bethe–Salpeter era), and the whole "13.6 eV" idiom of introductory and solid-state physics.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: e = \sqrt{2}\ \text{in Ry a.u.};\ \text{equivalently } e^2 = 2,\ e^2/2 = 1.\ \text{The Rydberg unit of charge is } e/\sqrt2 = 1.13288\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Papers literally write "e² = 2, m = 1/2, ħ = 1", which reads as a redefinition rather than a unit choice. In the Gaussian rendering only three generators are used (ħ, 2m_e, e²/2) and charge is derived with half-integer exponents (0.5, 1.5, -1, 0, 0).

per_symbol_rescalings.symbol: \mathbf B, \boldsymbol\mu (when a Gaussian rendering is used)
per_symbol_rescalings.relation: Same \alpha-type riders as Gaussian Hartree a.u., but with c = 2/\alpha = 274.072
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Rydberg-unit atomic-physics literature is usually Gaussian-flavored, so the magnetic ambiguity carries over with c doubled relative to Hartree a.u.

fingerprints: The literal triple "ħ = 1, m = 1/2, e² = 2" (or "2m_e = 1, e²/2 = 1")
Hydrogen Hamiltonian H = -∇² - 2Z/r — NO factor ½ on the kinetic term, and a 2 on the Coulomb term
E_n = -Z²/n² (not -Z²/2n²); ground state -1 rather than -0.5
Energies, cutoffs, forces and stresses quoted in Ry, Ry/bohr, Ry/bohr³: "ecutwfc = 60", "total energy = -123.456 Ry", "kinetic-energy cutoff 30 Ry"
Quantum ESPRESSO / PWscf output blocks; pseudopotential UPF files
c = 274.072 in relativistic terms (double the Hartree value)
Scattering cross sections in a₀² or πa₀² with energies in Ry; "threshold at 0.75 Ry"
Length unit is STILL bohr — a paper mixing bohr with Ry is Rydberg units, not Hartree units

benchmark_equations.coulomb: F = \dfrac{q_1q_2}{r^2},\qquad V = \dfrac{q_1q_2}{r},\ \text{with charges measured in units of } e/\sqrt2. The electron then carries q = -\sqrt2, so the electron-nucleus interaction reads V(r) = -\dfrac{2Z}{r}. Equivalently, in the Gaussian rendering e^2 = 2 and V = -Ze^2/r = -2Z/r.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: \nabla\cdot\mathbf E = 4\pi\rho, with \rho in units of (e/\sqrt2)\,a_0^{-3}. Poisson: \nabla^2\phi = -4\pi\rho. In electronic-structure codes the Hartree term is usually written v_H = 2\int \rho(\mathbf r')/|\mathbf r - \mathbf r'|\,d^3r' with \rho the ordinary electron density in e/bohr³ — the explicit leading 2 is the Rydberg signature.
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A: G is not a generator. Its numerical value in Rydberg a.u. is G = 1.9205\times10^{-42} = 8\times G_{\rm Hartree\ a.u.} (mass unit doubled, time unit doubled: G\,(2m_e)(2t_{\rm au})^2/a_0^3).
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: Schrödinger: i\dfrac{\partial\psi}{\partial t} = \left(-\nabla^2 - \dfrac{2Z}{r}\right)\psi,\qquad E_n = -\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}\ \mathrm{Ry}.\newline Dirac: \left[c\,\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf p + (\beta-1)\dfrac{c^2}{2} - \dfrac{2Z}{r}\right]\psi = E\psi with c = 2/\alpha = 274.071\,998, and m_ec^2 = \tfrac12 c^2 = 37\,557.730\ \mathrm{Ry} = 510\,998.95\ \mathrm{eV} (verified two independent ways).

systems.notes:
THE most important entry in this family for the tool, because Hartree and Rydberg atomic units are DIMENSIONALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE. E_h and Ry have identical dimension exponents (1, 2, -2, 0, 0); a₀ = 1 in both; ħ = 1 in both. A dimension-checker will validate H = -½∇² - Z/r and H = -∇² - 2Z/r equally happily. Only the recorded numeric factors (2 on the mass, 1/√2 on the charge) distinguish them. This is precisely the case the numeric_factor field exists for.

WHAT AGREES between Hartree and Rydberg a.u.: length (bohr, a₀ = 1 in both) and momentum (ħ/a₀ = 1 in both).
WHAT DIFFERS: energy (Ry = E_h/2), mass unit (2m_e vs m_e), time (Ry unit = 2 × Hartree unit = 4.8378e-17 s), velocity (Ry unit = ½ × Hartree unit), charge (e/√2 vs e), c (274.072 vs 137.036), and consequently force, pressure (Ry/bohr³ = 14710.51 GPa vs 29421.02 GPa), field strength, etc.
This mixed pattern — same length, half energy — is itself a good detector: a paper quoting a bond length in bohr and an energy that looks 2× a known hartree value is in Rydberg units.

CODATA 2022 values: 1 Ry = R_∞hc = 2.1798723611030e-18 J = 13.605693122990 eV = 109737.315681570 cm⁻¹ (this IS the Rydberg constant R_∞ = 10973731.568157 m⁻¹) = 157887.5124 K = 1312.7498197 kJ/mol = 313.7547370 kcal/mol = 3.2898419602500e15 Hz × h.

SPECTROSCOPIC SUBTLETY: R_∞ is the infinite-nuclear-mass Rydberg. Real hydrogen lines follow R_H = R_∞/(1 + m_e/m_p) = 109677.5834 cm⁻¹ (computed in-session from CODATA and matching the tabulated literature value exactly). Papers on hydrogenic spectra may mean either; the difference is 5.4×10⁻⁴ relative, far above modern spectroscopic precision.

MINOR RENDERING NOTE: some sources define Rydberg units in a 3-generator Gaussian form (ħ = 1, 2m_e = 1, e²/2 = 1) with no separate charge dimension; others use the 4-generator SI form above (ħ = 4πε₀ = 1, m = 1/2, e² = 2). Both are in current use; Quantum ESPRESSO documentation uses the latter. The two agree on every electric quantity and differ on magnetic ones exactly as in the Hartree case.
sources: Quantum ESPRESSO / PWscf documentation and community notes stating "e² = 2, m = 1/2, ħ = 1" and "all quantities are in RYDBERG ATOMIC UNITS" (https://elcorto.github.io/pwtools/written/background/pwscf.html; QE users list)

systems.name: Relativistic (Dirac) atomic units — ħ = m_e = c = 1
aliases: natural units of relativistic quantum mechanics
systems.used_in: Bound-state QED and Lamb-shift theory, Zα-expansion literature, strong-field QED and pair production, positronium and muonium theory, relativistic atomic structure formal work, high-intensity laser–electron interaction. Also the natural bridge to the particle-physics natural-units family.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: e = \sqrt{\alpha} = 0.085\,424\,5\ \text{(Gaussian rendering, } e^2 = \alpha\text{)};\ \text{or } e = \sqrt{4\pi\alpha} = 0.302\,822\ \text{(Heaviside-Lorentz rendering, } e^2 = 4\pi\alpha\text{)}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Once ħ = c = 1, charge is dimensionless and its value is fixed by α. Which of the two values appears depends on whether Maxwell's equations are rationalized. This is the same fork as in the particle-physics family and must be recorded, since e is not a free generator here.

fingerprints: "We use natural units ħ = c = m_e = 1" or "units in which ħ = c = 1 and masses are in units of the electron mass"
Zα appearing wherever Hartree a.u. would show Z: V = -Zα/r, (Zα)² expansions, "Zα expansion", "all-order in Zα"
Energies in units of m_ec² = 511 keV; "reduced Compton wavelength" ƛ_C = 386.159 fm as the length unit
Dirac ground state written E_{1s} = √(1 - (Zα)²) with no prefactor
Schwinger critical field written E_cr = m²/e = 1/√α, or in SI 1.323×10¹⁸ V/m
α appearing explicitly in places where Hartree a.u. would have 1

benchmark_equations.coulomb: V(r) = -\dfrac{Z\alpha}{r},\qquad F = \dfrac{Z\alpha}{r^2} (Gaussian rendering, e^2 = \alpha). In the Heaviside-Lorentz rendering V = -\dfrac{Ze^2}{4\pi r} with e^2 = 4\pi\alpha, which is numerically the same.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: Gaussian rendering: \nabla\cdot\mathbf E = 4\pi\rho. Heaviside-Lorentz rendering (more common in QED papers): \nabla\cdot\mathbf E = \rho. Both appear in this literature; the tell is whether e^2 = \alpha or e^2 = 4\pi\alpha.
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A as a set convention, but G IS expressible and dimensionless here: G = (m_e/m_{\rm Pl})^2 = 1.7518\times10^{-45}, since in \hbar = c = 1 units G carries dimension (mass)^{-2}. The field equations keep G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G\,T_{\mu\nu}.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: Dirac: \left[\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf p + \beta - \dfrac{Z\alpha}{r}\right]\psi = E\psi,\qquad E_{1s} = \sqrt{1 - (Z\alpha)^2}\ (\text{in units of } m_ec^2).\newline Nonrelativistic limit: i\partial_t\psi = \left(-\tfrac12\nabla^2 - \dfrac{Z\alpha}{r}\right)\psi,\ E_n = -\dfrac{(Z\alpha)^2}{2n^2}\ m_ec^2 (which for Z = 1, n = 1 gives -13.606 eV — verified numerically).

systems.notes:
Unit values: length ƛ_C = ħ/(m_ec) = 3.8615926744e-13 m = 386.159 fm = α·a₀ (verified: ƛ_C/a₀ = 7.2973525644e-3 = α to 9 figures); time ƛ_C/c = 1.28808866644e-21 s = α²·(Hartree a.u. of time); energy m_ec² = 8.1871057880e-14 J = 510998.95069 eV; momentum m_ec = 2.73092453e-22 kg m/s.

RELATION TO HARTREE a.u. — this is the cleanest way to remember it: Hartree a.u. and these units are related by powers of α. Length: L_rel = α L_Ha. Energy: E_rel = α⁻² E_Ha. Time: T_rel = α² T_Ha. So a converter can implement this as an α-scaling rather than a fresh generator solve, which is a useful cross-check on the linear-solve output.

OVERLAP WARNING: this system straddles the boundary with the particle-physics natural-units family (ħ = c = 1). Whichever family owns it, the tool must not register two conflicting entries. The distinguishing feature here is that the mass scale is m_e (not GeV, not m_Pl), so energies come out in units of 511 keV and lengths in fm-scale Compton units — a paper doing atomic/QED bound-state physics rather than collider physics.

Not to be confused with a supposed system "ħ = m_e = e = c = 1", which is INCONSISTENT: fixing all four would force α = 1. Any paper claiming it has made an error, or is silently working with a fictitious α.
sources: NIST CODATA 2022 listing: fine-structure constant, reduced Compton wavelength, electron mass energy equivalent, Planck mass
Derived in-session: ƛ_C/a₀ = α (9-figure agreement); E_n = -(Zα)²/2 × m_ec² reproduces -13.6057 eV for hydrogen; G = (m_e/m_Pl)² = 1.7518e-45
Standard bound-state QED literature convention (Zα expansion), e.g. Mohr, Plunien & Soff review conventions

systems.name: Effective (excitonic / material) atomic units — m* = 1, ε absorbed
systems.used_in: Semiconductor physics (shallow donors and acceptors, Wannier–Mott excitons, trions, biexcitons), quantum wells/wires/dots, 2D materials and TMD excitons, quantum Hall and 2DEG physics (via r_s), polaron theory, and by analogy in Rydberg-atom and cold-atom work. Also the muonic-atom and positronium literature, which uses the same reduced-mass rescaling.

per_symbol_rescalings.why: The mass generator is not a universal constant. Which mass is meant — band-edge m*, density-of-states mass, conductivity mass, or the exciton reduced mass μ = (1/m_e* + 1/m_h*)⁻¹ — is frequently left unstated, and the choices differ by factors of 2 or more.

Whether ε_r is the static ε₀ or the high-frequency ε_∞ changes Ry* by tens of percent (they differ by ~20% in GaAs, far more in polar and 2D materials). In 2D the Coulomb potential is not even 1/r (Rytova–Keldysh), so the rescaling is not a pure constant.

fingerprints: Symbols Ry*, R*, Ry_ex, a_B*, a*, a_X written with a star or asterisk
"in units of the effective Bohr radius / effective Rydberg"
Binding energies of 1–100 meV and radii of 1–20 nm (vs 13.6 eV and 0.053 nm)

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: k\in[-\pi,\pi]\ \text{when } a = 1\ \text{and } k = 2\pi/\lambda;\ \text{but many codes report } \mathbf k\ \text{in "crystal" / fractional coordinates } \mathbf k = \sum_i f_i\mathbf b_i\ \text{with } f_i\in[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]\ \text{and the } 2\pi\ \text{absorbed into } \mathbf b_i
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Whether the 2π lives in the Brillouin-zone boundary (π/a) or in the reciprocal lattice vector is a pure convention with no dimensional signature. VASP/QE k-point files, band-structure plots and analytic papers disagree.

A dimensionally invisible factor of 2 in the flux quantum, decided by whether Cooper pairs are involved. Hofstadter-butterfly and quantum-Hall papers use h/e; SQUID and vortex-lattice papers use h/2e. Both are called 'the flux quantum' and written Φ₀.

fingerprints: "we work in units where ħ = k_B = a = 1", "lattice units", "we set the lattice constant to unity"
Dispersions like ε(k) = -2t(cos k_x + cos k_y), with k dimensionless in [-π, π]
Conductance quoted in e²/h (= 3.874045865e-5 S) or 2e²/h; resistance in h/e² = 25812.80745 Ω (exact, von Klitzing)
"in units of e²/ħ" vs "in units of e²/h" — another silent 2π
Velocities in units of a t/ħ; times in ħ/t; "ħ/t = 1"
Green's functions G(k, iω_n) with Matsubara ω_n = (2n+1)πT — note T, not k_BT

benchmark_equations.coulomb: Usually SI or Gaussian, unmodified; more often the interaction is written as a Hubbard U on a site or a screened V_{ij}, and the microscopic Coulomb law never appears. When it does: V(r) = e^2/(\varepsilon r) with e^2 kept explicit or absorbed into a dimensionless coupling r_s.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A in most of this literature. Where electrodynamics is needed (e.g. axion electrodynamics, plasmonics) the paper reverts to SI or Gaussian explicitly.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: Tight-binding Schrödinger: i\dfrac{\partial c_i}{\partial t} = -t\sum_{\langle j\rangle}c_j + \varepsilon_i c_i;\quad \varepsilon(\mathbf k) = -2t\sum_{\mu}\cos k_\mu.\newline Continuum Dirac (graphene/TI): \hat H = v_F\,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf p\ \to\ \boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf k\ \text{when } v_F = \hbar = 1;\ v_F \approx 10^6\ \mathrm{m/s} \approx c/300 \text{ in graphene.}\newline Landau levels: E_n = \pm v_F\sqrt{2\hbar eB\,n}\ \to\ \pm\sqrt{2n}/\ell_B.

systems.notes:
The lattice constant a is a MATERIAL parameter, not a universal constant, so this cannot be a fixed generator table — the tool must accept a per-paper value (and a lattice type, since 'a' is ambiguous for non-cubic systems: conventional cell vs primitive cell vs nearest-neighbour distance; graphene's 'a' is 2.46 Å for the lattice constant but 1.42 Å for the C–C bond, and both are written a in the literature).

Useful anchors verified from CODATA 2022: von Klitzing constant h/e² = 25812.80745 Ω (exact); conductance quantum 2e²/h = 7.748091729e-5 S (exact); magnetic flux quantum h/2e = 2.067833848e-15 Wb (exact); ℓ_B = 25.6556 nm/√(B/T).

This entry composes with the k_B = 1 entry and with the model-Hamiltonian entry (t = 1, J = 1); in practice a condensed-matter paper declares all three at once in a single sentence. The tool should treat them as three independent switches rather than one monolithic system, because papers mix them freely (e.g. ħ = 1 but energies in meV, or t = 1 but temperature in kelvin).
sources: NIST CODATA 2022 complete listing (von Klitzing constant, conductance quantum, magnetic flux quantum — all exact)
Standard condensed-matter theory conventions; the h/e vs h/2e flux-quantum split is documented in both the quantum-Hall and superconductivity literatures
Derived in-session: ℓ_B numerical prefactor

systems.name: Model-Hamiltonian units (t = 1, J = 1, U/t)
systems.used_in: Hubbard and extended-Hubbard models, Heisenberg and Kitaev spin models, t-J model, Kondo and Anderson impurity models, DMRG/QMC/exact-diagonalization papers, frustrated magnetism, molecular magnetism (HDVV Hamiltonian), and Hückel/extended-Hückel molecular orbital theory.

generators.numeric_factor: 1, 2, \text{ or } -1\ \text{depending on the Hamiltonian convention (see rescalings)}

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \hat H = -2J\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\hat{\mathbf S}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf S}_j\ \text{(HDVV / molecular magnetism)}\quad\text{vs}\quad \hat H = -J\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\hat{\mathbf S}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf S}_j\quad\text{vs}\quad \hat H = +J\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\hat{\mathbf S}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf S}_j\ \text{(physics convention, } J>0 \text{ = antiferromagnetic)}.\ \text{Also } \sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\ \text{(each bond once) vs } \tfrac12\sum_{i\neq j}\ \text{(each bond twice)}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: THE canonical dimensionally-invisible disaster of this family. A reported J can differ by a factor of 2 (prefactor), another factor of 2 (double counting), and a sign, between two papers on the same compound. All four combinations appear in the literature. Molecular magnetism (Kahn) overwhelmingly uses -2J with J<0 antiferromagnetic; solid-state physics overwhelmingly uses +J with J>0 antiferromagnetic.

The sign of t is a gauge choice on a bipartite lattice (removable by a sublattice rotation) but NOT on a frustrated one, where it changes the physics. Papers that 'set t = 1' on a triangular lattice have made a physical choice, not a unit choice.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: E_k = \alpha + x_k\beta;\ \beta < 0\ \text{by convention};\ |\beta|\approx 2.7\ \mathrm{eV}\ \text{for graphene/benzene fits, but } \beta\ \text{is a FITTED parameter with no fixed value}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Hückel energies are quoted as pure numbers times β. Converting them to eV requires a β that is context-dependent (different for excitation energies, resonance energies, and band widths). The tool must refuse to auto-convert.

fingerprints: Axis labels and phase-diagram coordinates: U/t, J₂/J₁, T/t, T/J, Δ/t, W/t, J_K/D
"we set t = 1", "energies are measured in units of J", "all energies in units of the hopping"
Hamiltonians written with explicit -t, -2J, +J prefactors — read the prefactor, it is the convention
Hubbard: H = -t Σ c†c + U Σ n↑n↓; t-J: H = P(-t Σ c†c + J Σ (S·S - n n/4))P
Molecular magnetism: χT plots, "HDVV Hamiltonian", "J = -12 cm⁻¹" (note: J in cm⁻¹ is standard in that field)
Hückel: "α + 2β", "delocalization energy 0.472β"
Reported t in eV for real materials (graphene t = 2.7 eV; cuprates t = 0.4 eV, U = 8t)

Hubbard: \hat H = -t\sum_{\langle ijangle\sigma}\left(c^{\dagger}_{i\sigma}c_{j\sigma}+\mathrm{h.c.}ight) + U\sum_i n_{i\uparrow}n_{i\downarrow} - \mu\sum_i n_i.

ewline Heisenberg (HDVV / molecular-magnetism convention): \hat H = -2J\sum_{\langle ijangle}\hat{\mathbf S}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf S}_j,\ J<0\ 	ext{antiferromagnetic}.

systems.notes:
The prompt's instinct is right: these are per-model generators and must be handled as user-declared parameters, not as a fixed table.

But the deeper problem is that they are not ONLY unit conventions. Setting J = 1 is a unit choice; choosing between -2J Σ S·S and +J Σ S·S is an OPERATOR DEFINITION choice. The generator formalism handles the first and is silent on the second. My recommendation for the schema: the per_symbol_rescalings field can carry the relation (J_HDVV = -J_physics/2) as a string, which is what I have done, but the tool must present it as a warning requiring human confirmation rather than as an automatic transformation — the direction of the mapping depends on which paper you are reading, and there is no dimensional or textual signature that resolves it reliably. The only real evidence is the printed Hamiltonian.

The -2J vs -J vs +J confusion is well documented as a source of published errors in molecular magnetism (a factor of 2 or 4 in reported exchange constants between experimental and computational papers on the same compound is common). Treat this entry as the family's designated 'do not automate' zone.

Hückel theory is included here because α and β are literally energy generators set by fiat, but they are FITTED and non-transferable; there is no correct conversion of a Hückel energy to eV.
sources: Standard Hubbard/Heisenberg model literature conventions
O. Kahn, Molecular Magnetism (the -2J HDVV convention and its clash with the solid-state +J convention)

Verified only against convention statements in the literature, not against a single authoritative standard — no standards body has ever adopted a spin-Hamiltonian sign convention. Flagged as genuinely unresolvable without reading each paper's Hamiltonian.

systems.name: CGS-emu / Gaussian magnetism (gauss, oersted, emu)
systems.used_in: Experimental magnetism worldwide — SQUID and VSM magnetometry (Quantum Design MPMS/PPMS output is in emu), molecular magnetism and coordination chemistry (χ_M T plots in cm³ K mol⁻¹), permanent-magnet and soft-magnet engineering, thin-film magnetism, geomagnetism and rock magnetism, and a large fraction of the condensed-matter magnetism theory literature.

generators.numeric_factor: 1 (unrationalized: the 4\pi is written explicitly in the field equations, not absorbed)

per_symbol_rescalings.why: Pure unit scale; the safest conversion in the whole entry.

The 4π is dimensionless and enters here because CGS-emu is unrationalized. In vacuum B[G] and H[Oe] are numerically equal, which trains people to treat gauss and oersted as interchangeable — they are not, inside matter.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: 1\ \mathrm{emu\,cm^{-3}} = 10^{3}\ \mathrm{A\,m^{-1}};\ \text{note } 4\pi M\ \text{is often plotted "in gauss" because } B = H + 4\pi M
per_symbol_rescalings.why: emu/cm³ and gauss get used interchangeably for magnetization because 4πM has field units. The factor 4π must be tracked separately from the 10³.

'emu' is not a unit name in any coherent system — it is an abbreviation for 'electromagnetic unit' used as a placeholder for whatever the emu-subsystem unit of that quantity is. A SQUID reporting '3.2e-4 emu' means 3.2e-7 A m².

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: 1\ \mathrm{emu\,g^{-1}} = 1\ \mathrm{A\,m^{2}\,kg^{-1}}\ \text{(exactly, factor 1)};\ \text{but } 1\ \mathrm{emu\,g^{-1}} \to 4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{Wb\,m\,kg^{-1}}\ \text{if the Kennelly (polarization) SI form is used}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Two different SI targets for the same cgs quantity. The factor-1 route (A m²/kg) is the Sommerfeld convention and is the one to default to; several published conversion tables list only the 4π×10⁻⁷ route and mislead readers.
Dimensionless in both systems, differing by 4π. This is the single most frequently botched conversion in the magnetism literature.
4π plus a decade factor.
Molecular magnetism reports χ_M in 'emu/mol', which means cm³/mol. Note this quantity also carries the mole axis, compounding with the N-dimension problem.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: N_{\rm SI} = N_{\rm cgs}/4\pi;\quad \sum_i N_i = 4\pi\ \text{(cgs)} \ \text{vs}\ \sum_i N_i = 1\ \text{(SI)};\ \text{sphere: } N = 4\pi/3\ \text{vs}\ 1/3
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Dimensionless in both; differs by 4π. A demagnetizing correction applied with the wrong convention is wrong by 12.57×.
Straight scale factor.
Anisotropy constants K₁ are reported in erg/cm³ (older) or J/m³ or MJ/m³ (newer); permanent-magnet grades are still quoted in MGOe in the US market.
Both constants were derived in-session from CODATA; the famous '2.828' (= √8) is cgs-only. Applying it to SI χ_M is a factor-282 error and it does happen in print.

fingerprints: Units: G, gauss, Oe, oersted, emu, emu/g, emu/cm³, emu/mol, erg/cm³, Mx, maxwell, gilbert, MGOe
B = H + 4πM written as the constitutive relation; μ = 1 + 4πχ

μ_B quoted as 9.274e-21 erg/G rather than 9.274e-24 J/T
Instrument provenance: Quantum Design MPMS/PPMS, 'moment (emu)' column headings
Fields quoted in kOe (e.g. '50 kOe' = 5 T) rather than tesla
Demagnetizing factor for a sphere given as 4π/3 rather than 1/3

In the pure emu subsystem electric quantities are rescaled by c relative to esu and are essentially never used; magnetism papers that need electrostatics silently switch to Gaussian or SI.

ewline Constitutive relations (the ones that matter here): \mathbf B = \mathbf H + 4\pi\mathbf M,\quad \mathbf M = \chi\mathbf H,\quad \mu = 1 + 4\pi\chi,\quad \mathbf H_{m int} = \mathbf H_{m app} - N\mathbf M\ 	ext{with}\ \sum N_i = 4\pi.

systems.notes:
This literature is genuinely confused and the tool will add real value here. Every conversion above is a dimensionless 4π and/or a decade factor riding on top of the cgs↔SI length/mass/time change — exactly the case the schema's numeric_factor and per_symbol_rescalings fields exist for.

WHY IT IS SO CONFUSED: 'emu' is not a unit. In the CGS electromagnetic subsystem the unit of every quantity is 'the emu of <that quantity>', so 'emu' silently means erg/G for a moment, dimensionless for a susceptibility, and cm³ for a molar susceptibility. Instruments print 'emu' as a column heading with no quantity attached. A parser must infer the quantity from context before it can convert.

SECOND-ORDER TRAPS:
  - χ_M in 'emu/mol' means cm³/mol; χ in 'emu' with no denominator usually means the dimensionless volume susceptibility, but sometimes means moment/field = emu/Oe.
  - Molar susceptibilities carry BOTH the 4π problem and the mole-axis problem (see the quantum-chemistry entry). This is the one place in the family where two schema gaps compound.
  - Diamagnetic (Pascal's) constants are tabulated in units of 10⁻⁶ cm³/mol and must be subtracted before μ_eff is extracted; the sign convention (negative values tabulated as positive magnitudes) is inconsistent across tables.
  - Historical: the Weiss magneton μ_W ≈ μ_B/4.97 ≈ 1.853×10⁻²¹ erg/G appears in pre-1930 magnetism papers; it is an empirical unit with no modern standing.
  - Fields: 1 kOe = 0.1 T; 10 kOe = 1 T. Older papers use kOe throughout.

systems.name: SI magnetism — Sommerfeld vs Kennelly conventions
systems.used_in: Modern condensed-matter and materials papers using SI, permanent-magnet and electrical engineering (where Kennelly is common), IEC/ISO standards documents, and IUPAP/ISO-compliant journals. The Sommerfeld form is the one adopted by IUPAP, ISO 80000-6 and NIST.

per_symbol_rescalings.symbol: M vs J (magnetization vs magnetic polarization)
per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \textbf{Sommerfeld: } \mathbf B = \mu_0(\mathbf H + \mathbf M),\ [M] = \mathrm{A\,m^{-1}}.\qquad \textbf{Kennelly: } \mathbf B = \mu_0\mathbf H + \mathbf J,\ [J] = \mathrm{T}.\qquad \mathbf J = \mu_0\mathbf M
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Both are legitimate SI. A magnetization plotted 'in tesla' is a Kennelly J; a magnetization plotted 'in A/m' is a Sommerfeld M. They differ by μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ H/m exactly-by-definition-no-longer (μ₀ = 1.25663706127e-6 H/m, CODATA 2022, no longer exact since the 2019 redefinition).

per_symbol_rescalings.symbol: m vs j (magnetic moment vs magnetic dipole moment, Kennelly)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Two SI quantities both called 'the magnetic dipole moment', differing by μ₀. Older conversion tables list both SI targets for the same cgs source, which is why the emu tables look internally contradictory.

Every legacy conversion factor in the magnetism tables was computed with μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ EXACTLY. Since the 2019 SI redefinition μ₀ is a measured quantity. The discrepancy (1.6×10⁻¹⁰ relative) is far below any magnetism measurement, but a units engine claiming exactness must not.

'μ₀M' plotted explicitly, which is the tell that the author is aware of the fork

(BH)_max in kJ/m³ (SI) or MGOe (cgs); 1 MGOe = 7.957747 kJ/m³

Listed separately from the cgs-emu entry because the Sommerfeld/Kennelly fork exists ENTIRELY INSIDE SI and is invisible to a cgs↔SI converter. A tool that only knows 'gauss → tesla' will happily hand back a magnetization in tesla and never notice it has silently switched conventions.

There are no generators here — this is pure SI with a constitutive-relation choice. That is itself informative for the schema: the formalism needs a way to record 'no generators, but the symbol semantics differ', which is what the empty generators array plus populated per_symbol_rescalings expresses. systems.name: cgs-esu molecular electric property units (debye, Å³ polarizability, buckingham)
systems.used_in: Physical and computational chemistry (dipole moments, polarizabilities, hyperpolarizabilities), nonlinear optics, intermolecular-force and force-field parametrization, dielectric and solvation studies, molecular spectroscopy transition moments.

per_symbol_rescalings.why: The debye is an esu unit surviving inside otherwise-SI papers. Its exact SI value is 10⁻²¹/c, which is why it looks like an arbitrary decimal.

THE classic silent error: α in Å³ and α in C²m²J⁻¹ are NOT the same quantity — they differ by 4πε₀, which carries dimensions. A dimension-checker will correctly flag α[Å³] as a volume, which it literally is, and the tool must know that in this literature a 'volume' labelled α is an electric polarizability divided by 4πε₀.

Rarely stated; the buckingham is the natural esu quadrupole unit and appears without definition in intermolecular-force papers. Also, the quadrupole tensor itself has two conventions (traceless Buckingham Θ vs the primitive second moment), differing by a factor of 3/2 and a trace subtraction.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \text{a.u.: } \beta = 3.206\,361\,2996\times10^{-53}\ \mathrm{C^3m^3J^{-2}},\ \gamma = 6.235\,379\,9735\times10^{-65}\ \mathrm{C^4m^4J^{-3}}.\ \text{Convention fork: Taylor-series expansion } \mu = \mu_0+\alpha E+\tfrac{1}{2!}\beta E^2+\tfrac{1}{3!}\gamma E^3\ \text{vs perturbation-series } \mu = \mu_0+\alpha E+\beta E^2+\gamma E^3
per_symbol_rescalings.why: A reported β differs by a factor of 2 (and γ by 6) between the two expansion conventions, with no dimensional signature whatsoever. This is a documented, long-standing problem in comparing theoretical and experimental NLO hyperpolarizabilities. Additional forks: 'convention B' vs 'convention T' vs 'convention X'; and degeneracy factors for SHG vs EFISH vs THG.

'α in Å³' or 'polarizability volume'; values 0.2–20 Å³

benchmark_equations.gauss_law: \nabla\cdot\mathbf E = 4\pi\rho (esu). The polarizability-volume definition \alpha' = \alpha_{\rm SI}/(4\pi\varepsilon_0) is precisely the statement that the induced dipole in Gaussian units is p = \alpha' E with \alpha' a volume: for a conducting sphere of radius a, \alpha' = a^3 exactly.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: Response-theory definitions: \mu_i = \mu_i^{(0)} + \alpha_{ij}E_j + \tfrac{1}{2}\beta_{ijk}E_jE_k + \tfrac{1}{6}\gamma_{ijkl}E_jE_kE_l\ \text{(Taylor convention)},\ \text{with } \alpha_{ij} = -\left.\dfrac{\partial^2 E}{\partial F_i\partial F_j}\right|_{F=0} computed in atomic units and converted at the reporting stage.

systems.notes:
No generators — these are unit names and definitional riders that travel independently of any host system. Debye in particular appears inside SI papers, atomic-unit papers, and cgs papers indiscriminately.

The polarizability-volume issue is the sharpest test of whether a units engine understands this family. α[Å³] has dimension (0, 3, 0, 0, 0) — a pure volume. α[C²m²J⁻¹] has dimension (-1, -2, 4, 0, 2). They describe the same physical property. No dimensional analysis can connect them; only the recorded rider α' = α/(4πε₀) can. A tool that dimension-checks a paper reporting 'α = 1.45 Å³' against a formula containing α_SI will produce a spurious error unless this rider is in the table.

All numeric values above are CODATA 2022 atomic-unit entries read directly from the NIST listing; the a.u.→D, a.u.→Å³ and a.u.→buckingham ratios were computed in-session at 20-digit precision.

The hyperpolarizability convention fork is the one item in this entry I would NOT automate. It is a choice of Taylor coefficient, and papers frequently do not state it; the community's own review literature treats it as a persistent source of factor-2 and factor-6 discrepancies.

systems.name: Solid-state and DFT practical units (eV, Å, meV/atom, GPa, r.l.u.)

systems.notes:
Two distinct things are bundled here and the tool should keep them separate:
(1) REDUCED LJ UNITS are a legitimate three-generator system with per-model generators (ε, σ, m). Fully handled by the needs_custom_generators path, exactly like effective atomic units.
(2) SIMULATION-PACKAGE UNIT SETS (real, metal, electron, GROMACS, AMBER) are arbitrary, sometimes deliberately inconsistent, tuples of independent units. They are not generator systems at all; they are lookup tables. The right implementation is a hard-coded dictionary per package, not a linear solve.

The LAMMPS 'units electron' set is the sharpest cautionary tale in this family: energy in hartree, length in bohr, time in FEMTOSECONDS, mass in AMU. A reader (or a program) seeing hartree and bohr will conclude 'atomic units' and be wrong about time by 41.34× and mass by 1822.9×. Detection must never rest on two axes agreeing.

The AMBER 48.888213 fs time unit was derived in-session from √(u·Å²/(kcal/mol)) and matches the documented 1/20.455 ps.

systems.name: Magnetic-resonance units (NMR/EPR: ppm, Hz, gauss, MHz/T)
systems.used_in: NMR and EPR/ESR spectroscopy (experimental and computational), NMR crystallography, paramagnetic resonance in solids, quantum computing with spin qubits, MRI physics.

per_symbol_rescalings.why: Dimensionless, so dimensionally trivial — but the sign flip between the computed shielding σ and the reported shift δ, plus the choice of reference (TMS for ¹H/¹³C/²⁹Si, CFCl₃ for ¹⁹F, nitromethane vs ammonia for ¹⁵N — the last two differ by 380.5 ppm), makes it a real conversion problem the tool can help with.

Hyperfine couplings are reported in MHz (modern EPR, and computation), in gauss or mT (older EPR, field-swept spectra), and in cm⁻¹ (optical/magneto-optical work). The MHz↔mT conversion is g-DEPENDENT, so it is not a pure unit conversion — it requires the g-value of the species.
Field-swept EPR spectra are indexed by B; the conversion to energy requires g. Derived in-session.
J is nucleus-pair-dependent; K is the nucleus-independent quantity used for comparing computed couplings across isotopes. Converting between them requires both magnetogyric ratios.
γ and γ/2π are both called 'the gyromagnetic ratio' and differ by 2π — dimensionally invisible. CODATA lists both (γ_p = 2.6752218708e8 s⁻¹T⁻¹ vs γ_p/2π = 42.577478461 MHz/T).

The single generator is h = 1 (energies expressed as frequencies), which is shared with the spectroscopic-equivalence entry. What makes this a separate row is that several of the 'conversions' are NOT unit conversions at all — they require a physical parameter (g-value, magnetogyric ratio, reference compound). The tool must model these as parameterized conversions and refuse to run them without the parameter.

Specifically: MHz ↔ mT for a hyperfine coupling is g-dependent; ppm ↔ Hz is spectrometer-frequency-dependent; J ↔ K is isotope-pair-dependent. A units engine that treats 'MHz to gauss' as a fixed factor will be wrong for every species with g ≠ 2.0023, which includes essentially all transition-metal and lanthanide complexes (g from 1.4 to 10+).

systems.name: Historical X-ray and spectroscopic length units (X unit, kX, ångström star; air vs vacuum wavelengths)
systems.used_in: Pre-1950 X-ray crystallography and X-ray spectroscopy (lattice constants and wavelengths in kX), X-ray wavelength metrology up to the 1990s (Å*), and — still today — atomic line lists and astronomical spectroscopy, where wavelengths above 200 nm are conventionally quoted in air.

per_symbol_rescalings.why: Siegbahn's 1925 x unit was INTENDED to be exactly 10⁻³ Å but is about 2 parts per 1000 larger. Every pre-1947 crystallographic lattice constant published 'in Å' is really in kX and is therefore ~0.2% too small when read as ångström. There are TWO x units (Cu and Mo anchored), differing from each other by 2.2×10⁻⁵ relative.

An intermediate practical scale used for X-ray wavelengths from 1965 until direct SI-traceable measurements superseded it. Values on the Å* scale differ from SI ångström in the 5th decimal — irrelevant for structure but not for X-ray metrology.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \lambda_{\rm vac} = n(\lambda, T, p, \text{humidity})\,\lambda_{\rm air};\ n \approx 1.000\,277\ \text{at 500 nm, 15\,°C, 101.325 kPa, dry air (Edl\'en 1966 / Ciddor 1996)}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: NOT a constant factor: n depends on wavelength, temperature, pressure and humidity. This is genuinely outside a multiplicative-generator formalism and requires a dispersion formula. Convention: NIST ASD and classical line tables give AIR wavelengths above 200 nm and VACUUM below; wavenumbers are always vacuum.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \text{Pre-1960: } 1\ \mathrm{\AA}\ \text{defined via the red Cd line} \ (\lambda = 6438.4696\ \mathrm{\AA}\ \text{in dry air, 15\,°C, 760 mmHg}).\ \text{Since 1960: } 1\ \mathrm{\AA} \equiv 10^{-10}\ \mathrm{m}\ \text{exactly}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: A pre-1960 ångström is not exactly 10⁻¹⁰ m. The difference is ~10⁻⁷ relative, negligible for chemistry, relevant only in metrology archaeology.

'Å*' or 'ångström star' — X-ray wavelength tables 1965–1990s

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: these are length-unit definitions with no physical-law content.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: N/A: no dynamical content. The relevant relations are metrological: Bragg's law n\lambda = 2d\sin\theta (unit-agnostic, which is exactly why a kX/\AA{} confusion propagates silently from \lambda into d); and \tilde\nu = 1/\lambda_{\rm vac}.

systems.notes:
Marked UNSUPPORTED deliberately, and the reason is instructive for the schema.

The kX/xu/Å* part IS a plain multiplicative rescaling of a length and could be handled as a unit definition (with the caveat that xu comes in Cu- and Mo-anchored flavours). But the air/vacuum wavelength convention is a WAVELENGTH-DEPENDENT, non-multiplicative transform requiring the Edlén or Ciddor dispersion formula plus ambient conditions. No generator table, and no linear system over dimension exponents, can express it. It belongs in a numeric-converter module with an explicit refractive-index model, not in the units formalism.

This is the family's clearest example of a convention that a dimensional-analysis engine must recognize and REFUSE, rather than approximate. Recommend the tool detect the air-wavelength convention (a spectroscopic wavelength above 200 nm quoted to 4+ decimals, or the phrase 'air wavelength') and emit a warning with the ~0.03% magnitude of the effect rather than silently treating λ_air as λ_vac.

CODATA 2022 values for xu(Cu Kα₁), xu(Mo Kα₁) and Å* read directly from the NIST listing. These are among the few CODATA entries that carry significant uncertainty (2.8e-7 and 9.0e-7 relative), which itself signals that they are legacy conversion factors rather than defined units.

Practical relevance today: reading pre-1950 structural literature (0.2% lattice-constant offsets), and reading atomic line lists (air/vacuum). Both are real, both are v2.

family_notes:
CROSS-SYSTEM OBSERVATIONS, TRAPS, AND WHERE THE GENERATOR-TABLE SCHEMA BREAKS

=== 1. THE DEFINING PROBLEM OF THIS FAMILY: DIMENSIONALLY INVISIBLE FACTORS OF 2 ===

Hartree and Rydberg atomic units are DIMENSIONALLY IDENTICAL. E_h and Ry have the same exponent tuple (1,2,-2,0,0); a₀ = 1 in both; ħ = 1 in both; momentum unit ħ/a₀ = 1 in both. A dimension-checker will validate H = -½∇² - Z/r and H = -∇² - 2Z/r with equal enthusiasm. This is not an edge case — it is the family's central hazard, and it recurs at every level:
  - Hartree vs Rydberg atomic units (factor 2 in energy)
  - Hartree-like vs Rydberg-like EFFECTIVE atomic units (same factor 2, even less often declared)
  - h vs ħ, ν vs ω, ν̃ vs k (factor 2π, four times over)
  - Flux quantum h/e vs h/2e (factor 2, decided by whether Cooper pairs are involved)
  - Heisenberg -2J vs -J vs +J, and Σ_<ij> vs ½Σ_{i≠j} (up to factor 4 and a sign)
  - Hyperpolarizability Taylor vs perturbation expansion (factor 2 in β, 6 in γ)
  - Atomic unit of intensity with and without the ½ (factor 2)
  - Susceptibility χ_SI = 4πχ_cgs and demagnetizing N_SI = N_cgs/4π (factor 4π, twice)
The numeric_factor and emits fields are not a convenience here — they are the entire information content that distinguishes half these systems.

Diagnostic tip worth building in: Hartree and Rydberg a.u. AGREE on length and momentum and DISAGREE on energy, time, velocity, mass, charge and pressure. That asymmetric signature (bohr present, energy 2× off) is a reliable detector. Concretely: a.u. pressure = 29421.016 GPa vs Ry/bohr³ = 14710.508 GPa; c = 137.036 vs 274.072.

=== 2. WHERE THE 5-TUPLE (M, L, T, Θ, I) IS INSUFFICIENT ===

(a) AMOUNT OF SUBSTANCE IS MISSING. kcal/mol, kJ/mol, cm³/mol, J mol⁻¹K⁻¹, eV/atom, meV/atom, eV/f.u. all carry a per-amount divisor with true SI dimension N⁻¹. Under the 5-tuple, 1 kcal/mol and 1 kcal are indistinguishable — a silent 6.022×10²³ error, the largest available in this family, in the single most-used reporting convention in chemistry. STRONG RECOMMENDATION: add an optional sixth exponent N, with N_A as the generator that collapses it. The 'per atom' and 'per formula unit' divisors are integer cell counts, not N_A, and need a separate slot again.

(b) RECIPROCAL RELATIONS ARE NOT LINEAR RESCALINGS. E = hc/λ maps energy to wavelength by inversion, not multiplication. No linear solve over dimension exponents can produce it. The spectroscopic converter needs an explicit graph with one reciprocal edge (energy ↔ wavelength) alongside the multiplicative ones (energy ↔ cm⁻¹, Hz, K, eV, J/mol).

(c) SOME CONVENTIONS ARE NOT DIMENSIONAL AT ALL. Air-vs-vacuum wavelength is a wavelength-, temperature-, pressure- and humidity-dependent transform (Edlén/Ciddor). Watson A- vs S-reduced Hamiltonians are different effective operators. Hückel α/β are fitted, non-transferable parameters. In each case the correct behaviour is to DETECT and REFUSE, not to approximate. The schema's 'unsupported' value should be used freely here.

(d) MATERIAL PARAMETERS AS GENERATORS. Effective atomic units (m*, ε_r), lattice units (a), model units (t, J), and reduced LJ units (ε, σ, m) all have generator tables that are structurally identical to the universal-constant systems but whose entries are per-paper numbers. The 'needs_custom_generators' path must accept these as user input; there is no default that is not wrong.

=== 3. THE MAGNETIC α AMBIGUITY (worth its own alarm) ===

'Atomic units' is ambiguous by a factor of α ≈ 1/137 in EVERY magnetic quantity, and by nothing at all in every electric one. The SI-based atomic unit of magnetic flux density is ħ/(ea₀²) = 2.35051757077×10⁵ T; the Gaussian-based one is e/a₀² = 1.7152555×10³ T = 1.7152555×10⁷ G. I verified in-session that the ratio is exactly α (α × 2.35051757e5 T = 1715.2555 T, and e/a₀² computed independently in Gaussian units = 1.71525554e7 G — agreement to 8 figures).

The ONLY reliable textual discriminator is whether magnetic terms carry an explicit 1/c: H_Z = (1/2c)(L+2S)·B (Gaussian) vs H_Z = ½(L+2S)·B (SI-based). A paper stating 'in atomic units, B = 0.1' with no Hamiltonian is unresolvable. Recommend a hard warning rather than a conversion.

=== 4. RATIONALIZATION IS NOT WHERE PEOPLE EXPECT IT ===

Setting 4πε₀ = 1 makes Coulomb's law rationalization-free (F = q₁q₂/r²) but puts 4π BACK into Gauss's law (∇·E = 4πρ, since ε₀ = 1/4π). Both Hartree atomic units and Gaussian units share this. Heaviside–Lorentz atomic units (∇·E = ρ, e² = 4πα) are essentially absent from AMO/quantum-chemistry literature and I would not implement them; they appear only where this family touches QED.

Half-integer dimension exponents appear exactly where a system is Gaussian-rendered: charge = M^½L^{3/2}T⁻¹ = (0.5, 1.5, -1, 0, 0). Both renderings of the same physical system must be supported and must be known to be the same system — Hartree a.u. is a 4-generator integer-exponent system in its SI rendering and a 3-generator half-integer system in its Gaussian rendering, with identical physics.

=== 5. COMPOSABILITY: THESE ARE NOT MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE SYSTEMS ===

Real papers stack conventions. A condensed-matter paper may declare ħ = 1, k_B = 1, a = 1, t = 1 in one sentence — four independent switches. A quantum-chemistry paper computes in Hartree a.u., reports energies in kcal/mol, dipoles in debye, polarizabilities in Å³ and temperatures in kelvin, all in the same table. A magnetism paper reports fields in tesla, moments in emu, susceptibilities in cm³/mol and exchange constants in cm⁻¹.

The tool should therefore model these as COMPOSABLE MODIFIERS, not as a flat list of mutually exclusive systems. In particular k_B = 1 is orthogonal to everything else in the family: it is the only generator here that touches Θ, and no atomic-unit system includes it by default. 'T = 0.001 in atomic units' means 315.8 K; 'T = 300' in the same paper almost certainly means kelvin. Flag, do not guess.

=== 6. HYBRID / DELIBERATELY INCONSISTENT UNIT SETS ===

LAMMPS 'units electron' (hartree + bohr + FEMTOSECOND + AMU) is the cautionary example: two axes look like atomic units and two are not, off by 41.34× in time and 1822.9× in mass. Detection must never rest on two axes agreeing. Simulation-package unit sets (LAMMPS real/metal/electron, GROMACS, AMBER) are lookup tables, not generator systems, and should be hard-coded as such.

=== 7. VERIFICATION METHOD USED ===

I downloaded the NIST CODATA 2022 complete listing (allascii.txt, 366 lines) and read every relevant constant directly rather than from memory. Every derived number in this table was then recomputed in-session at 20-significant-figure precision and cross-checked against CODATA's own relationship entries. Independent checks that all passed:
  - m_ec² computed as ½(2/α)² Ry = 37557.7301 Ry = 510998.95 eV, matching CODATA's electron mass energy equivalent
  - ƛ_C/a₀ = 7.2973525644e-3 = α to 9 figures
  - Gaussian a.u. of B computed two ways (α × SI value, and e/a₀² in cgs) agreeing to 8 figures
  - R_H = R_∞/(1+m_e/m_p) = 109677.5834 cm⁻¹, matching the tabulated literature value exactly
  - E_n = -(Zα)²/2 × m_ec² reproducing -13.6057 eV for hydrogen
  - Rotational-constant magic numbers 505379.008 MHz·u·Å² and 16.857629 cm⁻¹·u·Å² derived from h and m_u
  - AMBER's 20.455 recovered as √(u·Å²/(kcal/mol))⁻¹ = 48.888213 fs
  - μ_eff prefactors 2.827869 (cgs) and 797.727 (SI) derived from CODATA
Magnetism conversion factors were taken from the canonical NIST/Goldfarb–Fickett table (fetched in-session via Lake Shore's reproduction) and spot-checked by independent derivation; note that one commonly-circulated version of that table garbles the specific-magnetization row (1 emu/g = 1 A m²/kg exactly in the Sommerfeld convention; the 4π×10⁻⁷ factor belongs to the Kennelly Wb·m/kg target).

=== 8. ITEMS I AM GENUINELY UNCERTAIN ABOUT ===

  - The exact prevalence of the 3-generator Gaussian vs 4-generator SI rendering of RYDBERG atomic units. Quantum ESPRESSO documents the 4-generator form (ħ = 4πε₀ = 1, m = ½, e² = 2); older atomic-physics literature is Gaussian. I have recorded both but have not established which dominates.
  - The hyperpolarizability convention fork: I am confident the fork exists and that β differs by 2 and γ by 6 between Taylor and perturbation conventions, and I cite Willetts et al. (1992) from knowledge — I did not re-verify that reference in-session.
  - The Weiss magneton value (μ_B/4.97) is from memory and was not verified against a primary source; it is historical trivia and low-stakes.
  - Pre-1960 ångström definition details (Cd red line value) are from memory.
  - Whether any current literature uses Heaviside–Lorentz atomic units. I found none and believe it is empty, but cannot prove a negative.

=== 9. SCOPE RECOMMENDATION SUMMARY ===

v1 (build first): Hartree a.u. (both renderings), Rydberg a.u., effective/excitonic a.u., quantum-chemistry molar units, k_B = 1, spectroscopic energy equivalences, cgs-emu magnetism, SI magnetism conventions, cgs-esu molecular properties (debye/Å³), solid-state eV–Å units.
v2 (build second): relativistic ħ = m_e = c = 1, molecular-constant conventions, condensed-matter ħ = k_B = a = 1, model-Hamiltonian units, MD simulation unit sets, magnetic-resonance units, historical X-ray length units.
No entry in this family is out of scope for a tool aimed at theoretical-physics reading, but the model-Hamiltonian sign conventions and the air/vacuum wavelength transform should be surfaced as warnings rather than automated conversions.
